scope: Project device support packages; ordinary applications are classified separately
delivery: Cumulative unstable COPR kernel, followed by DNF; physical acceptance precedes provider removal

groups.reason: Kernel, modules and DT are already versioned together; retain the accepted recovery kernel.

SPI, firmware lifecycle, contact decoding and input publication belong in the native NT36532 driver. Require both panel suppliers, all contacts, pen/gestures and suspend/recovery before withdrawing the legacy client. Local private assets remain separate.

Move supported SSC/QMI transport, units, discovery and lifetime into IIO. Native motion/light/proximity/temperature exist; dual-light, matrix, SAR, vendor diagnostics and physical lifecycle remain admission gates.
Keep the standard D-Bus frontend. Stock IIO must supply correct motion axes, both ALS semantics, proximity and restart behavior before replacing the SSC-specific rebuild.
The DSP requests filesystem/registry services through FastRPC. Native IIO still depends on this firmware service. Do not add kernel filesystem parsing or private calibration packaging.
Qualified transport and physical channel semantics can enter IIO. Diagnostic capture, uncertainty reporting and unqualified CCT/flicker interpretation remain userspace.
The native platform_profile/QoS provider replaces the old backend. Keep the original distribution power-profiles-daemon and persistent user selection.

Telemetry models, D-Bus, user thresholds and offline UI remain userspace; electrical limits, ownership and supported power_supply controls belong in the kernel. Preserve existing disabled qualification gates and preferences.

Threshold error propagation, health estimation and late sysfs discovery are daemon defects. Fixing a kernel driver cannot replace these checks or justify fabricated capacity. Review original distribution compatibility before retiring the rebuild.

Move sensor axes and hardware reporting to DT/IIO. Keep desktop preferences, DDC permissions, original desktop integration and GPU statistics frontend in userspace. Suspend and block-scheduler selection are system policy.
MSM binding, clocks, firmware requests and resource ownership belong in the kernel/DT. The historical render-only module override is not a permanent hardware driver.

DRM color properties, panel commands and register programming belong in kernel. The profile/firmware generator and color preference remain userspace; DMA/HDR activation keeps its existing admission gates.
OpenGL/Vulkan/OpenCL compilers and rendering APIs are userspace. Keep fixes narrow; move actual DRM/MSM hardware defects to the kernel rather than moving Mesa itself.
Codec firmware, V4L2 controls, formats and DMA belong in kernel drivers. VA-API translation, GStreamer/PipeWire negotiation and session policy remain userspace.

Sensor/CAMSS/clock/EEPROM/actuator drivers belong in kernel/DT. libcamera/IPA, image tuning and autofocus algorithms remain userspace. Both fitted calibrated cameras and rear focus/parking remain required.
Audio graph/session negotiation and speech processing remain userspace. Codec, amplifier, DSP transport and protection enforcement belong in ALSA/kernel; preserve gain and calibration gates.

Load and validate device-private read-only calibration through the native protected ALSA ABI. Keep parsing and persistent files out of the kernel; the kernel owns transport, graph admission, mandatory limiting and fault muting. Native audio acceptance remains required.
ALSA controls and hardware safety are kernel-owned. UCM, WirePlumber routing, orientation-dependent channel selection and desktop controls remain userspace.
FM19511 and IR SPI/encoders are already kernel drivers. Retain command-line tools and device permissions; they are not duplicate drivers.

The kernel owns UART/HCI/regulators and the normal address interface. Protected factory addresses currently live in read-only persist files, not a demonstrated NVMEM cell. Do not encode unique addresses in public DT or teach kernel drivers to parse filesystems.
Pogo transport, HID/input, backlight and power ownership belong in kernel. Factory credential loading, firmware admission and desktop session preference remain separate userspace responsibilities.

Keep redistributable firmware separately versioned and loaded by request_firmware; device-private calibration stays local/read-only. Embedding blobs in Image does not remove their licensing or update responsibilities.
DNF transactions, signed package admission, staging, filesystem setup, RTC persistence and recovery are userspace. Preserve automatic staging, rollback preference and the recovery route.
Control API, settings and native user interfaces consume kernel capabilities; preferences and privileged authorization do not belong in DT.
Dependency selection and upgrades require RPM metadata. Retire old provider requirements only after the replacement capability and solver/upgrade/recovery checks pass.

Original distribution KDE/GNOME packages are required by workspace policy. Generic desktop/library defects cannot be transplanted into DT; validate dependency closure and preserved settings for replacement.
Binder, namespaces and networking primitives belong in kernel and are already queued. Container setup, images, application integration and diagnostics remain userspace.

Keep only fixtures required by active source/build dependencies and concise signed evidence. Retire completed temporary packages after those dependencies are removed; never install fixture packages as drivers.
Applications and compiler runtimes cannot be implemented in kernel/DT.
